At what temp $\left(\mathrm{V}_{\text {rms }}\right)_{\mathrm{H}_{2}}$ is same as $\left(\mathrm{V}_{\text {rms }}\right)_{\mathrm{O}_{2}}$ at temperature 47°C.
(1) 94 K
(2) 293 K
(3)20 K
(4) 40K

steps:
$\mathrm{V}_{\text {rms }}=\sqrt{\frac{3 R T}{M}}$
$$\begin{array}{l}
\frac{V_{\mathrm{H}_{2}}}{V_{\mathrm{O}_{2}}}=1=\sqrt{\frac{3 R T_{\mathrm{H}_{2}}}{3 R T_{\mathrm{O}_{2}}}} \times \sqrt{\frac{M_{\mathrm{O}_{2}}}{M_{\mathrm{H}_{2}}}} \\
\Rightarrow \sqrt{\frac{T_{\mathrm{H}_{2}}}{(273+47)} \times\left(\frac{32}{2}\right)}=1 \\
\Rightarrow T_{\mathrm{H}_{2}}=\frac{320}{16} \\
\Rightarrow T_{\mathrm{H}_{2}}=20 \mathrm{~K}
\end{array}$$

A particle of mass m is projected at an angle of 30° with initial velocity $u$. Find its angular momentum about point of projection at maximum height.
(1) $\frac{\mathrm{mu}^{3}}{4 \mathrm{~g}}$
(2) $\frac{\sqrt{3}}{16} \frac{\mathrm{mu}^{3}}{\mathrm{~g}}$
(3) $\frac{\sqrt{2} m u^{3}}{2 g}$
(4) $\frac{\sqrt{3} m u^{3}}{2 g}$

steps:
Angular momentum from point of projection
$$\begin{aligned}
\mathrm{L}_{0} & =\mathrm{mv} \mathrm{r}_{\perp} \\
& =\mathrm{m}\left(\mathrm{u} \cos 30^{\circ}\right) \mathrm{H} \\
& =\mathrm{m}\left[\mathrm{u} \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right]\left[\frac{\mathrm{u}^{2} \sin ^{2} 30}{2 \mathrm{~g}}\right] \\
& =\mathrm{m}\left[\mathrm{u} \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right]\left[\frac{\mathrm{u}^{2}}{8 \mathrm{~g}}\right]=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{16} \frac{\mathrm{mu}^{3}}{\mathrm{~g}}
\end{aligned}$$

questions.text:
Resistance of roster at 27°C is $60 \Omega$. Temperature coefficient of resistance is $\alpha=2 \times 10^{-4} \operatorname{Per}{ }^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$. Find temperature of resistance when voltage and current across resistance will be 210 Volt and 2.75 A .
(1) 1250 °C
(2) 890 °C
(3) 1693 °C
(4) 2015 °C

steps:
$\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{t}}=\frac{\mathrm{V}}{\mathrm{l}}=\frac{210}{2.75}=80$
$$\begin{array}{l}
R_{t}=R_{0}(1+\alpha \Delta t) \\
80=60(1+\alpha \Delta t) \\
20=60 \alpha \Delta t \\
\Delta t=\frac{20}{60 \alpha} \\
\Delta t=\frac{1}{3 \times 2 \times 10^{-4}}=\frac{10^{4}}{6}=1666^{\circ} \mathrm{C} \\
t_{f}=1666+27=1693^{\circ} \mathrm{C}
\end{array}$$

A particle travels 125 m with change in velocity as 50 m/s in t to (t + 1) second. Find the displacement in $(\mathrm{t}+2)^{\mathrm{th}} \sec$.
(1) 100 m
(2) 175 m
(3) 225 m
(4) 275 m

steps:
Displacement in $(\mathrm{t}+1)^{\mathrm{th}}$ second
$$\begin{array}{l}
125=u+\frac{a}{2}(2 t+1) \\
\Rightarrow \quad 125=u+\frac{50}{2}(2 t+1) \\
\Rightarrow \quad 125=u+25(2 t+1) \\
\Rightarrow \quad 125=u+50 t+25 \\
\quad 100=u+50 t
\end{array}$$
$$\begin{array}{l}
S_{t+2}=u+\frac{a}{2}(2(t+2)-1) \\
S_{t+2}=u+25(2 t+3) \\
S_{t+2}=100+75=175 m
\end{array}$$

If a $L-R$ circuit power factor is $\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ for $E=25 \sin (1000 t)$. Then power factor for $E=20 \sin (2000 t)$ will be.
(1) $\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}$
(2) $\frac{1}{\sqrt{7}}$
(3) $\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$
(4) $\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

steps:
Power factor for first alternating EMF
$$\begin{aligned}
\cos \phi= & \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}=\frac{R}{\sqrt{R^{2}+\omega^{2} L^{2}}} \quad \text { where } \omega=\text { angular frequency of first } E M F \\
R & =\omega L
\end{aligned}$$

For second alternating EMF we can say that angular frequency of second alternating EMF is double of first alternating EMF
∴ angular frequency for second alternating EMF $\omega_{2}=2 \omega$
Now power factor for second EMF
$$\begin{array}{l}
\text { P.F. }=\frac{R}{\sqrt{R^{2}+4 \omega^{2} L^{2}}} \\
\because R=\omega L \\
\therefore P . F .=\frac{R}{\sqrt{5} R}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}
\end{array}$$
